exampleAnswers.title: Determining the Lengths of the Major and Minor Axes of an Ellipse

question.text: What are the lengths of the major and minor axes of the ellipse above?
question.explanation:
The major axis is the longest diameter of the ellipse, which is the line segment bounded by the points $(-0.5, -6)$ and $(-0.5, 2).$ So, the length of the major axis is $2 - (-6) = 8.$

The minor axis is the shortest diameter of the ellipse, which is the line segment bounded by the points $(-2,-2)$ and $(1,-2).$ So, the length of the minor axis is $1 - (-2) = 3.$

exampleAnswers.title: Determining the Lengths of the Semi-Major Axis of an Ellipse

question.text: What is the length of the semi-major axis of the ellipse given above?
question.explanation:
The major axis is the longest diameter of the ellipse, which is the line segment bounded by the points $(2,1)$ and $(2,-4).$ So, the length of the major axis is $1 - (-4) = 5.$

The length of the semi-major axis is half the length of the major axis. So, the length of the semi-major axis is $\dfrac{5}{2} = 2.5.$

question.text: What is the length of the semi-major axis of the ellipse given above?
question.explanation:
The major axis is the longest diameter of the ellipse, which is the line segment bounded by the points $(3,-1)$ and $(3,-9).$ So, the length of the major axis is $|-9 - (-1)| = 8.$

The length of the semi-major axis is half the length of the major axis. So, the length of the semi-major axis is $\dfrac{8}{2} = 4.$

exampleAnswers.title: Determining the Lengths of the Semi-Minor Axis of an Ellipse

question.text: What is the length of the semi-minor axis of the ellipse above?
question.explanation:
The length of the semi-minor axis is half the length of the minor axis.

  • The minor axis is the shortest diameter of the ellipse, which is the line segment bounded by the points $(-3,1)$ and $(1,1).$ So, the length of the minor axis is $1 - (-3) = 4.$

  • The length of the semi-minor axis, then, is $\dfrac{4}{2} = 2.$
